Germ mode bacteria detection

Summary of the uploaded 22-page file: how Germ mode counts bacteria, the R&D re-test of four samples, and its agreement with culture and a Sysmex analyzer. Every fact and number here comes from that file. From file marks original pictures, New graphic marks charts and diagrams drawn here from the file's numbers.

Pages 1–2

How Germ mode works

Hint details: how Germ mode works
  • Settling principle: bacteria are smaller than other formed elements, so they settle more slowly. When the other elements are ready for imaging, some bacteria are still above the imaging region and can be missed.
  • Layers: the 1 mm chamber is imaged in 40 layers. Studies found bacteria only in layers 1–30.
  • Measure and predict: cocci and bacilli are counted in the four layer-scan images (layers 1–4). The pattern is matched to a library of distribution curves, which predicts layers 5–30. Cocci plus bacilli give the total concentration.
  • Image capture: each sample gets 60 segmented images plus 4 layer-scan images.
  • 488/µL rule: above 488/µL, one extra 40× image is shown. It is display only and not used in the count. Steps 01–05 run on every sample.
  • Normal mode: no layer scans. Result = segmented-image count × 2.68 per µL.
  • False-positive claim: the file says the settling difference between bacteria and small crystals reduces false positives, with a marked improvement only in certain atypical samples.

Bacteria are smaller than other formed elements, so they settle more slowly. When the other elements are ready for imaging, some bacteria remain above the imaging region and may be missed. Studies of the 1 mm counting chamber (40 layers) found bacteria only in layers 1–30. Germ mode counts bacteria in layers 1–4, then predicts layers 5–30 from a library of distribution curves.

  1. Urine sample
    In counting chamber; bacteria settle slowest
  2. Capture 60 + 4 images
    60 segmented images and 4 layer-scan images
  3. Count by layer
    Cocci and bacilli in scan layers 1–4
  4. Apply distribution curve
    Layer pattern picks the curve; covers layers 5–30
  5. Add cocci + bacilli
    Total concentration (Germ mode)
  6. Report result
    particles/µL; if bacteria > 488/µL, one extra 40× image is shown (display only, not used in the count)

New graphicMeasure layers 1–4, predict layers 5–30

Measured, layers 1–4Predicted, layers 5–30

Because bacteria and small crystals settle differently, the algorithm combines measurement with the library prediction. The file states this lowers false positives, and that Bacteria Mode gives a marked improvement only in certain atypical samples. Normal mode takes no layer scans: its result is the segmented-image count × 2.68 per µL.

Hint details: R&D re-test
  • Scope: R&D tested 18 urine samples. The hospital's issue was reproduced in samples 02, 06, 07 and 09. The file does not describe the issue itself.
  • Table: Germ vs Normal mode total is 397.9 vs 323.9 (02), 717 vs 281.1 (06), 2,507.8 vs 307.9 (07), 2,066.3 vs 310.6 (09). Samples 07 and 09 are mostly bacilli (2,129.1 and 1,866.2 /µL) with cocci at 378.7 and 200.1 /µL.
  • Per-layer counts (sum of layers 1–4): sample 02 has 2 bacteria, 06 has 6, 07 has 34, 09 has 26.
  • File's explanation: samples 07 and 09 have relatively high counts in every layer, so their final concentrations are high. The final concentration comes from the layer counts and the matching distribution curve.
  • Scan images: the instrument labels detected objects COCCI or LUS (the file's bacillus label).

Deep explanation: how to read pages 3 and 4
  • Column groups on page 3: the green frame is the image counts (total bacteria in images, cocci, bacilli). The blue frame is the Germ mode concentration in /µL (total, cocci, bacilli). The right-hand red frame is the Normal mode total in /µL. Left-hand columns are in Chinese: sample ID, sample type, run mode and 20× fields (60 for every sample).
  • Internal checks that hold in every row: cocci count + bacilli count = total image count (for example 3 + 118 = 121), and Germ cocci + Germ bacilli = Germ total (for example 8 + 389.9 = 397.9).
  • Normal mode is a straight multiple: Normal total ÷ image count is 2.68 in every sample with a non-zero count (for example 323.9 / 121 = 2.68; 8 / 3 = 2.67). This matches the page 4 note that Normal mode is about 2.68 × the segmented-image count.
  • Germ mode is not a straight multiple: the four highlighted samples have almost the same image count (105–121) and almost the same Normal result (281–324 /µL), yet Germ mode gives 398, 717, 2,508 and 2,066 /µL. So Germ mode is driven by something other than the 60 segmented images: the four layer scans and the distribution curve.
  • Layer scans separate the four samples: sample 02 has 2 bacteria across all four layers and sample 06 has 6, while 07 has 34 and 09 has 26. Sample 07 still has 8 bacteria in layer 4 and sample 09 has 5. The file says high counts in each layer explain the high final concentrations of 07 and 09.
  • Not proportional to the layer total: 2 → 397.9, 6 → 717, 26 → 2,066.3 and 34 → 2,507.8 /µL. The file says the layer pattern picks a distribution curve, but it does not give the formula, so the exact mapping cannot be checked from the file.
  • The highlighted gap alone does not define the issue: samples 05 and 08 also show Germ mode far above Normal mode (5,943.3 vs 728.2 and 4,784.9 vs 578.3 /µL) but are not highlighted. The file says only that the hospital's issue was reproduced in 02, 06, 07 and 09, so what the issue was is not stated.
  • Few / Moderate labels: four green and orange labels sit beside the Normal mode column on page 3: Few, Few, Moderate, Moderate. The file does not define them. Their arrows point toward the highlighted rows in order, but the exact link is not stated.
  • Repeated value 192.8: Germ bacilli /µL is exactly 192.8 in samples 03, 12, 16, 20 and 21, where the bacilli counts are 9, 6, 2, 4 and 1. Germ cocci in sample 04 is also 192.8. The file does not explain this repeat.
  • Cocci vs bacilli split: in the layer scans, sample 07 has 20 cocci and 14 bacilli, yet its Germ concentrations are 378.7 cocci and 2,129.1 bacilli /µL. Sample 09 shows the same pattern (11 cocci, 15 bacilli in scans; 200.1 and 1,866.2 /µL). The file does not say how the split is carried into the final concentration.
  • Zero sample: sample 13 is 0 in every column, so a zero count gives zero in both modes.

The file holds the same four layers for samples 02, 06 and 09 on pages 5–12 and 17–20.

Page 21 of the PDF has its metric values in a different order from its headers when the text is extracted. The values above follow the counts in the table (for example 65/73 = 89.04% sensitivity, 202/217 = 93.09% specificity) and match the page as displayed.
Hint details: performance results
  • Cutoff: both comparisons use 1429/µL.
  • Versus culture (290): 65 shared positives and 202 shared negatives; 15 extra Germ-mode positives and 8 misses. Sensitivity 65/73 = 89.04%, specificity 202/217 = 93.09%, agreement 267/290 = 92.07%.
  • Versus Sysmex (403): 22 shared positives and 369 shared negatives; 10 extra EH-2090 positives and 2 misses. Sensitivity 22/24 = 91.67%, specificity 369/379 = 97.36%, agreement 391/403 = 97.04%.
  • Error rates: false-positive rate = extra positives / all reference negatives. False-negative rate = misses / all reference positives. Culture: 6.91% and 10.96%. Sysmex: 2.64% and 8.33%.
  • Correlation: slope 1.0253, R² 0.8708, shown as the equation and points only; the file adds no comment.
Source: uploaded file “Germ_mode_pdf.pdf”, 22 pages. New graphics use only numbers printed in that file; the settling curve is a schematic.
